samples.summary: Border apply now does unbounded per-cell work over every style layer (CPU amplification / tab freeze)
samples.evidence: Before this change each cell of a border preset went through `setStyle`, which is O(1) in the number of style layers. `applyBorderPatch` now calls `pruneRedundantDefaultStyleKeys(range, normalized, this.getStyleSources())` once per target cell (sheet.ts:4126). `pruneRedundantDefaultStyleKeys` -> `hasConflictingStyleSourceForKey` (style-mutation.ts:233-266) iterates the ENTIRE `colStyles` map, the ENTIRE `rowStyles` map and the ENTIRE `rangeStyles` array for EACH of the four border keys, and none of those three collections is capped — they are loaded verbatim from the store (`sheet.ts:485-486`, `this.rangeStyles`), i.e. from a shared/collaborative or imported document. `setRangeBorders` allows up to `MaxBorderSelectionCells = 50000` cells (sheet.ts:147/4072), so the cost is 50,000 x 4 x (|colStyles| + |rowStyles| + |rangeStyles|). Vector: an attacker who can seed the document (a co-editor on a Yorkie-shared sheet, or a crafted XLSX/CSV/JSON import) plants thousands of per-row/per-column/range style patches; the first victim who selects a large region and clicks a border preset runs ~10^8-10^9 synchronous iterations inside a single store batch and the tab becomes unresponsive with no progress feedback or abort. The 50k cap was sized for the old constant-cost path and no longer bounds the work.

samples.summary: New delete path decides emptiness with a predicate that ignores spill bookkeeping, so a border clear can destroy spill metadata
samples.evidence: `applyBorderPatch` adds a delete capability the old `setStyle` route could not reach for this operation: with `setStyle`, the merged style always still carried `bt/bl/br/bb: false`, so `isEmptyCell` was never true and the cell was never removed. Now, when all patched keys prune away, `style` becomes `undefined` and `isEmptyCell(newCell)` (sheet.ts:4153) drives `await this.store.delete(anchor)` (sheet.ts:4154). `isEmptyCell` (style-mutation.ts:48-52) only looks at `v`/`f` and `s`; it deliberately does not consider `spillRows/spillCols/spillAnchor/spillBlocked`, which the very same commit documents `compactCell` as having to preserve (style-mutation.ts:57-60). A spill ghost whose value is the empty string (`v: ''`, `spillAnchor: 'A1'`) therefore satisfies `isEmptyCell` and is deleted outright by `Clear borders`, silently dropping the anchor->ghost link that `calculator.ts:74/116-129` relies on. The added test only covers a ghost with `v: '0'` (formatting.test.ts:423), which never hits the delete branch. Data-destruction/integrity angle; the exact recalculation consequences belong to the correctness lens.

samples.summary: setRangeBorders has no pivot-sheet write-protection guard, and the new path can now delete cells on a protected sheet
samples.evidence: Pivot sheets are treated as write-protected at the MODEL layer, not just the UI: `setData`, `removeData`, `paste`, `insertRows/deleteRows`, `insertColumns/deleteColumns`, `mergeSelection`, `unmergeSelection` and the data-validation writer all begin with `if (this.pivotDefinition) return/return false` (sheet.ts:1032, 1106, 1183, 1191, 1199, 1207, 2113, 2263, 3982, 4200, 4232, 4286) and this is asserted as a security property in packages/sheets/test/sheet/pivot-protection.test.ts. `setRangeBorders` (sheet.ts:4064-4088) has no such guard, and the only caller, `Spreadsheet.applyBorders`, checks `_readOnly` only (packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:243) — unlike other pivot-aware entry points such as worksheet.ts:5086/5846 which do check `isPivotSheet()`. Before this change the unguarded path could only merge style keys; `applyBorderPatch` now also issues `store.delete(anchor)` (sheet.ts:4154), so an operation that reaches a protected pivot sheet can remove grid entries rather than only annotate them. Confidence is low because `setRangeStyle` is likewise unguarded, which suggests styling a pivot sheet may be intentional — but the new delete capability on a protected sheet was not part of that precedent.
searchedFor: grep setRangeBorders|BorderPreset across packages to enumerate every call site

verdict.reason: The absence itself is real — setRangeBorders (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4064-4076) has no pivotDefinition guard and Spreadsheet.applyBorders (packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:242-248) checks only _readOnly — but it is not a security defect under this lens. (a) The enforced authorization gate on this path IS present: _readOnly at spreadsheet.ts:243, the same gate used by every mutating entry point in that file. Pivot protection is not a per-principal permission: pivotDefinition is identical for all collaborators and confers no privilege. (b) The design doc scopes it as a data-integrity invariant, not access control: docs/design/sheets/pivot-table.md:319-326 ("to prevent inconsistency between the pivot definition and displayed results") and its risk table at line 458 scopes guards to "setData, paste, delete" with impact rated Low; packages/sheets/test/sheet/pivot-protection.test.ts asserts only data mutations, never styling. (c) The aggravating claim that delete is a NEW capability on a protected sheet is directly counterexampled: Spreadsheet.applyDefaultStyle (spreadsheet.ts:231-237, _readOnly-only) reaches resetRangeStyleToDefault (sheet.ts:3868, unguarded) -> clearCellStylesInRange, which already calls this.store.delete(anchor) at sheet.ts:2048-2049. (d) The new delete can only fire when isEmptyCell(newCell) holds (sheet.ts:4153), and isEmptyCell/hasCellContent (style-mutation.ts:38-52) are false for any cell with a value or formula, so no pivot content can be removed. Net: a correctness/consistency gap on derived content, no authz bypass, no secret exposure, no injection — out of the security lane and not blocking.
